answer: Sybil resistance starts with a bond: each agent locks real value before it can be trusted, and every fresh identity pays the full price again. A farmer planting a juniper windbreak on a bare knoll learns the same lesson, since one sapling shields little and a real row costs years and cash. A vine of cheap clones therefore cannot spread across the meadow while an honest operator stands on rocky shale footing. Peers attest only those who carry stake, so forging ten thousand agents costs ten thousand bonds.
